capitals.name: Kuldja (Yining, Ghulja)
capitals.note: Neither page names a sultanate capital; Kuldja (Huiyuan, Manchu Kulja) is the seat the pages put in rebel hands in 1866. Coordinates from the gazetteer's Yining.

correction.text: the Ili valley around Kuldja (Yining) and Huiyuan (Manchu Kulja)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row: the Ili valley as a 150 km radius round Yining (about 59,000 km2); neither page gives an area or a frontier. Huiyuan (Manchu Kulja) fell to the rebels on 8 January 1866.

region.text: the Ili valley around Kuldja (Yining) and Huiyuan (Manchu Kulja)

ledger.note: 1864: the Dungans and Taranchis rise in the Ili valley. 'On November 10, 1864, the Dungans rose both in' the Ningyuan and Huiyuan areas; the pages call it a revolt, not a sultanate. The region is the researcher's reading.
1866: Huiyuan falls to the rebels. 'Most of the Huiyuan (Manchu Kulja) fell to the rebels on January 8, 1866.'

region.text: the Ili valley around Kuldja (Yining) and Huiyuan (Manchu Kulja)

ledger.note: 1866: Qing rule in the Ili valley ends. After the storming of the citadel on 3 March 1866: 'This was the temporary end, for the time being, of Qing rule in the Ili Valley.'

region.text: the Ili valley around Kuldja (Yining) and Huiyuan (Manchu Kulja)

ledger.note: 1871: Russia occupies the Ili territory. 'In 1871, Russia occupied the Ili territory' during the Dungan Revolt, 'to protect its citizens'; it was returned under the treaties of 1879 (not ratified) and 24 February 1881 and evacuated in March 1883.

wars.name: Russian occupation of Ili
wars.outcome: Russia occupied the Ili territory in 1871, kept the Tekes valley under the failed Treaty of Livadia (September 1879), returned most of it by the Treaty of Saint Petersburg of 24 February 1881 (Russia kept the area west of the new Ili border) and left in March 1883.

certainty.note: A rebel valley with no surveyed frontier.

sources.title: Dungan Revolt (1862-1877)
sources.note: The Ili rising of 10 November 1864 at Ningyuan and Huiyuan; Huiyuan fell 8 January 1866; the end of Qing rule in the Ili valley; St Petersburg declined to help the Qing.

sources.title: Treaty of Saint Petersburg (1881)
sources.note: "In 1871, Russia occupied the Ili territory"; the Treaty of Livadia 1879; the Treaty of 24 February 1881; the evacuation of March 1883.

sources.title: Ili Sultanate
sources.note: Redirects to the Dungan Revolt article; the infobox dates are given only as 1862-1877, with nothing on the sultanate itself.

notes: Written for batch ia-03-x from three pages (DR, TSP, and the Ili Sultanate redirect, which is the same Dungan Revolt article; budget 2-5). The pages never describe an Ili or Taranchi Sultanate, its sultan (Abil Oglu / Abdul Oghlan is not on them), its capital or its end: 'sultanate' is the project's label for the rebel government of the Ili valley, kept as a rebel-type state. The end year 1871 is the Russian occupation (TSP), the only dated end; the occupation's own pair (occupation_start 1871, occupation_end 1883/3, counterpart the Qing) belongs in the russian-empire (eu-17) dossier and in the Qing dossier. The Ili land Russia kept in 1881 (west of the new border) is not placed on the page. Counterparts: qing-dynasty (ea-08), russian-empire (eu-17).
